findings.claim: A commit replaced an accurate comment with one claiming the state is shallow-cloned and that in-place mutation of a nested value would corrupt initialState and break reset(), but the code actually performs a full deep copy on store creation and again on reset(), so initialState cannot be corrupted and reset() still works; this gives readers an incorrect mental model of the store and should be reverted or reworded to state only what is true.

The requestUrl handling supports string, URL, and Request inputs, but the tests only exercise the string case even though the app's CGW client, built on RTK's fetchBaseQuery, calls fetch with a Request object, meaning the branch the app actually uses (input.url) is untested; if that branch broke, unit tests would still pass and the only symptom would be an unexplained timeout in the tx-send-cgw-failure Maestro run.
The same assertion (expect(request.params.chainId).toBe(`eip155:${…}`)) appears on both line 587 and line 590, apparently left over from an edit, and the duplicate line should be removed.

A commit removed ticket references from e2e comments, but this file still contains a comment referencing the ticket's 'Add a signer' CTA not existing in the implementation, which should be deleted or reworded to remove the ticket mention.

The suite header still describes only a 'pairing & session-approval suite', but the suite now also includes connected-apps management flows and transaction-request flows, so the header should be updated to reflect all three groups.

E2E_TX_OWNER_ADDRESS duplicates the first owner address from mockData.ts instead of referencing it, and a recipient address (0x81BdB0…) is repeated as a raw string at two other locations rather than a named constant, so if the fixture Safe's owners change these copies will silently drift and break the tx flows without an obvious cause.
